sections.h2: Where to find the Charlevoix County Register of Deeds
sections.html:
The office is at 13513 Division Street in the city of Charlevoix, MI 49720. The phone is 231-547-7204, the fax is 231-237-0106, and email goes to rod@charlevoixcounty.org. Call before you drive in, because public counter hours are not posted online.

The city of Charlevoix is the county seat, while Boyne City is the largest city. Whether you are selling a Lake Charlevoix cottage, a place in East Jordan or a home on Beaver Island, the transfer finishes at this one office. It is a constitutional office created in 1835 that records, indexes and preserves land documents.

sections.h2: What happens to your deed after it arrives
sections.html:
Staff stamp the time on it, give it a liber and page, scan it and add it to the searchable index. That sequence puts the buyer's name on the public record for the property.

Recording does not make a document legal; it makes the document public. Counter staff have no blank deed forms to hand out and cannot draft or coach, because MCL 600.916(1) bars clerks from giving legal advice. The deed itself comes from your closing attorney or the title agent, and the register of deeds only checks it against the recording rules.

  • Deeds, mortgages, land contracts and discharges are recorded here.
  • The computer image index reaches back to January 1984, and older records are still being indexed.
  • Documents can be walked in or mailed with the fee and a prepaid return envelope.

For a mailed package, send the signed original deed, one check for the fee and any tax, the treasurer's certificate if the deed needs one, and a prepaid return envelope. Staff cannot record a deed that is missing a required piece, so a complete package saves a second round of mail before your closing.

Filing one document costs $30.00 whatever its length. That amount follows MCL 600.2567, and $4.00 of it is sent to the Michigan State Survey and Remonumentation Fund.

Charlevoix County Register of Deeds statutory fees

One check payable to the Charlevoix County Register of Deeds can cover the recording fee, any transfer tax and the tax certification together. Since January 2, 2025, the office adds $3.00 per document for return postage when you send a document in without a prepaid return envelope, and it holds the document unrecorded until that amount arrives.

sections.h2: What transfer tax comes due at a Charlevoix County closing?
sections.html:
Most sales carry two taxes, both counted in $500 slices of the price with any leftover treated as a full slice. MCL 207.504 sets the county rate at 55 cents a slice for counties under 2,000,000 people. MCL 207.525 puts the state rate at $3.75 a slice.

The full value has to appear on the deed itself, or an affidavit stating it travels with the deed. For a sale at $276,800, the typical owner-occupied value here, that is 554 slices.

Some transfers escape the county tax. MCL 207.505 lists instruments with consideration under $100, security instruments such as mortgages, leases, and deeds that only fix a title flaw. Ask the office how your own deed is treated well before the closing date.

sections.h2: Layout rules that can bounce a deed
sections.html:
A deed must satisfy the page rules in MCL 565.201, and the office may not take one that misses them. Formatting causes most returns, so inspect the sheet before it goes in the mail.

  • Margin: 2.5 inches of clear space at the head of page one and half an inch around the rest of every page.
  • Print: 10-point type or bigger, black ink, white paper of 20-pound stock or heavier.
  • Size: letter or legal sheets only, from 8.5 by 11 up to 8.5 by 14.
  • First line: one statement naming the recordable event, such as warranty deed.
  • Only one recordable event per instrument.

The statute also wants a legible printed name under every signature that matches the acknowledgment, and the name and workplace address of whoever drafted anything signed after 1964.

sections.h2: Why do I need a tax certificate before a warranty deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Michigan law makes the office ask for proof that no tax liens attach to the parcel. Under MCL 211.135 the county treasurer certifies that taxes for the five years leading up to the deed date are paid, and Charlevoix charges $5.00 for that certification.

The deeds that trigger this step are warranty deeds, covenant deeds, land contracts, and trustee, fiduciary or personal representative deeds with a warranty clause. It reaches master deeds for condominiums as well. A quitclaim deed with no warranty covenants is excluded by MCL 211.135(6)(e), so it moves through without the certificate.

Start at the County Treasurer's Office, then bring the certificate with the deed. If you owe back taxes, settle them before the closing date so the certificate can be issued.

sections.h2: Searching records and guarding your title
sections.html:
The county offers three search routes and a free fraud alert. Webtecs is the free portal for taxpayers and occasional users, and images can be bought document by document. Laredo Anywhere is a subscription service for people who run title searches regularly; email rod@charlevoixcounty.org to request an agreement. Tapestry is a web search that needs no subscription.

Homeowners can also enroll in Property Fraud Alert, which sends the owner an alert whenever a filing appears under their name. That helps after a sale too, since a seller can watch for a deed or lien appearing against a property they believed they had cleared.

sections.h2: Charlevoix County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Charlevoix County is one of the pricier corners of northern Michigan. It has about 26,036 residents and 18,026 housing units. Owners live in 83.5% of occupied homes, median rent is $949, and the typical household brings in $76,531.

In the 2020 count, 35.4% of housing units sat vacant, which points to plenty of seasonal and second homes. Water covers 70% of the county's 1,390 square miles, so waterfront parcels and island properties often carry details that the deed and title search have to capture accurately.

faqs.q: What is the filing charge for one deed in Charlevoix County?
faqs.a: One document costs $30.00 whatever its length. A tax certification adds $5.00 when the deed type calls for one, and a mailed document with no prepaid return envelope adds $3.00 for postage. Transfer tax is separate and follows the sale price.

faqs.q: Can the Charlevoix County office prepare my deed for me?
faqs.a: No. Staff cannot draft papers or give legal advice, since MCL 600.916(1) bars clerks from it, and the office keeps no blank deed forms. Have an attorney or the title agent prepare the deed first.

faqs.q: Do I need a tax certificate for a quitclaim deed in Charlevoix County?
faqs.a: Usually not. MCL 211.135(6)(e) exempts a quitclaim deed or other conveyance with no covenants of warranty from the certificate rule. Warranty deeds, covenant deeds, land contracts and certain fiduciary deeds do need the County Treasurer's certification first.

faqs.q: How do I pay the transfer tax on a Charlevoix County sale?
faqs.a: Pay when you hand in the deed. Make transfer tax and tax certification checks out to the Charlevoix County Register of Deeds; one check can cover them together with the recording fee. Rates are 55 cents (county) and $3.75 (state) per $500 slice.

faqs.q: Where can I buy a copy of a recorded Charlevoix deed?
faqs.a: Search the free Webtecs portal and buy the image, or ask the office. Plain copies are $1.00 a page and certified copies are $5.00, so request the exact total on a long document.
